gaps.status: open, with three routes and an order of preference. (1) The cheapest and the strongest: whichever objective the operator actually traps with demonstrably passes 1064 nm at a working numerical aperture, which is a functional observation -- operator_read, E3, and not E1, since E1 needs a run_id from this system. Nobody has said which objective that is; that is a question for the operator. (2) An endpoint value read off the published curve BY THE OPERATOR is operator_read at E3, at decade precision only, and it is a fact about the endpoint wavelength rather than about 1064 nm. (3) A caller that needs 1064 nm anyway records its own extrapolation as an assumption at E5, naming this gap, with the authorisation for it recorded on the assumption rather than on any entry -- being told to use a value is not evidence for it, and if an authorisation could lift E5 to E3 the grade scale would become a permission scale. No route allows a curve to be extrapolated past its endpoint inside the store.
gaps.note: MRD70170 (10x) is absent from nearest[] because no transmittance curve has been supplied for it at all -- for that part the gap is absent rather than condition_mismatch.

label_warning: Selector labels in the vendor configuration are not authoritative. Three known traps on this instrument, in increasing order of how quietly they fail. (1) In the source project one branch selector's label-to-state mapping was inverted in the configuration file and stayed wrong for weeks, because both the label and the state read back consistently -- only an image showed which position passed light. (2) csuw1_disk_position's two labels are confocal and bright field, but the bright-field position also serves widefield fluorescence, so the configuration id cannot be recovered from the label and a read-back that agrees with the label confirms nothing about which configuration is loaded. (3) csuw1_port has three slots whose order is unknown, and two of the three send zero light to one camera: commanding position 2 for the dichroic may land the mirror, and read-back will confirm position 2 and tell you nothing. O1 preflight therefore verifies state by read-back and, where a selector decides whether light arrives at all, by acquiring. Drivable and readable is not the same as verifiable, and those are two properties rather than one field.

It is csuw1_port, an element of a channel that is automatable in full with read-back, and it is drivable and readable through micromanager. automatable_gaps: [camera_splitter] is gone from widefield_inline, widefield_side and transmitted, and with it the 2.1 rule 5 manual instruction sheet on those three.

resolved_gaps.what_it_does_not_resolve: the element can now be SET without a human, but it still cannot be VERIFIED by read-back alone, because two of its three states starve one camera. The old automatable_gaps field bundled setting and verifying together and only one of them is gone.

note_on_the_confocal_unit_in_every_path: The unit's dichroic stays in the path whatever the disk does, which is why this instrument has no unfiltered white-light path, and its port still chooses the camera. What the disk position selects is whether the light is confocally sectioned on the way through. Two separate facts about one unit, and conflating them was the first reading of the extracted dossier -- the third such conflation, after the port with the splitter and the bright-field selector with the disk position.
